closed_custody_json_patch.value: Parent closure 2026-10-15 (operator decision A applied to a measurement-coverage blocker; sixth closure): CLOSED `spreadsheetbench / dataset-journal-gap`. The operator confirmed, after the parent filed the clause-by-clause candidate in registry/blocker-closure-assessment.md, that reading A covers the one remaining PENDING-RUN clause: eligible/selected/task/trial/invalid/unmeasured coverage is a precondition on a future separately authorized diagnostic, not a condition on closure - exactly as reasoning_gym closed with no measured run. Every other clause was already satisfied, and the last PENDING-WORK clause was discharged the same day by w-spreadvacuous. (1) Authenticated row-level gradable eligibility: registry/w-spreadelig-eligibility.md classifies all 400 installed rows - 394 structurally gradable without a run, 1 (`283-32`) retained only by the explicit official-range-zero compatibility policy, 5 not gradable as installed with a per-row reason; 794/800 workbooks open in both openpyxl modes and all 800 ZIP/XML structures are readable. (2) Complete installed workbook/mirror authentication and the bounded first-five selected-only packet: registry/w-jc2-review.md, registry/w-spreadrt-runtime.md, tests/fixtures/hg_wsel/spreadsheetbench.json. (3) The synthetic stale-cache formula-conversion failure is FIXED, not waived: w-spreadcache traced the cause to LibreOffice's own load policy (default OOXMLRecalcMode=1 at /usr/lib/libreoffice/share/registry/main.xcd:724); the shipped check now forces mode 0 in a private profile, strips scalar formula caches from a private ZIP copy and requires regenerated caches before the converted file may replace the candidate, so a stale-cache workbook is unmeasured rather than published as a measured score, and the opt-in real-engine control preserves the authored [999,888] -> [5,10] bar. (4) The vacuous-pass soundness hole is FIXED: a released answer_position whose range expands to zero cells (`'Sheet1'!BD2:308`; parse_cell_range gives an end column of 0) made cell_level_compare iterate nothing and return True, so a released row published an unperformed 1.0 measurement for any submission. w-spreadvacuous (commit 803ef598) makes an empty expansion exit 3 with a named reason and no reward file, and names an unaddressable component instead of skipping it; the released colon-range parser ValueError stays a measured zero exactly as before. The scorer digest is now 98dd625481f091a8684dd4d7a66c17f07cf7a36c8bba160e27353e06988b1af7 and is bound in this file's own observed field; registry/w-spreadrt-runtime.md is retained unedited as the dated e7131a26... pre-fix observation, and the superseded cache-only binding 5c247413... is recorded as dropped in the integration, not silently lost. (5) The one-released-variant named-cell metric statement and the official-range-zero compatibility policy are satisfied and recorded in registry/w-metriccmp-comparability.md and registry/w-spread2-reconciliation.md; the local score is not identified with the upstream three-variant soft_restriction mean or hard_restriction all-pass aggregate. (6) Failed receipts, missing engine package archives and the conditional native/replay and read-only result-path observations remain preserved as explicit bounded limits, and the withdrawn shared requirements (scorer-offline-closure, artifact-only-state-export, pristine-verifier, runtime-observations) stay withdrawn rather than re-imposed. THIS CLOSES NO MEASUREMENT AND CLAIMS NO SCORE: spreadsheetbench has never had a measured run here, no coverage count is promoted, measured/selected/trial/invalid/unmeasured and run_id stay null, and no diagnostic or pilot is authorized by this closure. The retained coverage obligation, the fresh bounded no-model regressions with real engine invocation, correct fresh cached values and explicit network isolation, and the reconciliation of any diagnostic manifest with the first-five packet all remain preconditions on a future, separately authorized diagnostic that must use its own fresh run ID and the current staged policy.
